concepts.why: Name vs passages / secular scholar: 1 John 3:12 never mentions an offering (Cain's murder and the deeds of the two brothers only), so the name says more than that passage does. Drop it, or rename the concept with a plain label such as 'Abel and Cain'. Notes on Gen 4:3-5 and Heb 11:4 are exact. (Heb 11:4 'by faith' beside 1 John 3:12 'deeds' would have been a fine unharmonised pair under a name that covers it.)

concepts.name: Abraham offered Isaac
concepts.why: Name vs passages: 'God Himself will provide the lamb' is said only in Gen 22:7-8 (and echoed in 22:14); Gen 22:2, Heb 11:17-19 and James 2:21 are about Abraham offering Isaac, not about a lamb being provided. Rename in the texts' words (James 2:21 'offered his son Isaac on the altar'; Heb 11:17 'offered up Isaac'); the Gen 22:7-8 note keeps the provide-the-lamb phrase. Lutheran / Reformed / Catholic readers: James 2:21 is the verse at the centre of the faith-and-works dispute; under a name about the lamb it reads as chosen to make a point, under 'Abraham offered Isaac' it is simply a text that says so. Notes are exact.

Name vs passages and Lord's Supper: 1 Cor 10:18 says 'those who eat the sacrifices', not 'peace offering'; putting it under this name asserts that the sacrifices Israel ate were peace offerings and reads as the first half of the Lord's Supper argument (10:16-21), on which Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed and Baptist readers part. Drop it here (it can live in a concept that says what it says, see missing).

Name vs passages / secular scholar: 'The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit' is said only by Ps 51:17. Ps 34:18, Isa 57:15 and Isa 66:2 speak of the contrite and the humble but never of sacrifice; they share a word, not the concept. Drop them (or, if they are wanted, rename the whole concept 'A broken and a contrite heart', which then no longer speaks of sacrifice). Consider extending Ps 51:16-17 to 51:16-19 so the psalm's own turn, 'then You will delight in righteous sacrifices', stands with it rather than only in the secondary list (Jewish readers will not take Ps 51 as a rejection of sacrifice).

concepts.name: Better than sacrifice
concepts.why: Name vs passages: 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' is Hos 6:6 and the two Matthew quotations; 1 Sam 15:22 says obedience, Prov 21:3 righteousness and justice, Mark 12:33 love of God and neighbour, Micah 6:8 justice, mercy and walking humbly. The common words are 'better than' / 'more than sacrifice' (1 Sam 15:22 'better than', Prov 21:3 'more desirable than', Mark 12:33 'more important than'). 'Better than sacrifice' (a plain label with 1 Sam 15:22's words) fits all seven; the Hosea line remains the note on Hos 6:6. Jewish and Catholic/Orthodox readers also gain: it does not say sacrifice is abolished.

note_fixes: Hebrews 10:4-9: trim to Hebrews 10:4-8; verse 9 ends 'He takes away the first to establish the second', which is more than this concept needs and is the one sentence in the concept that states how the old and the new stand to each other
concepts.why: Name vs passages: only Ps 40:6-8 and Heb 10:5-8 (a quotation of it) say 'did not desire'. Ps 50:8-13 says 'I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices' and 'I have no need'; Jer 7:21-23 says what God commanded ('Obey Me'). Move Jer 7:21-23 to concept 18 (it is the same point as 1 Sam 15:22) and Ps 50:8-13 either to a concept of its own ('If I were hungry, I would not tell you') or beside Ps 50:14. Original arbitrates: Ps 40:6 says 'my ears You have opened' while Heb 10:5 says 'a body You prepared for Me' (Hebrews quotes the Greek version); the packet shows both verbatim, which is right, but nothing in the name or notes may say they are the same text. Scholar and Jewish readers would object if a note did. Notes are exact.

note_fixes: Acts 8:32-35: trim to Acts 8:32-33. Verses 34-35 are Philip answering 'who is the prophet talking about' with 'the good news about Jesus', so the passage itself says Isa 53 is about Jesus; a concept that sets that beside Isa 53 and Jer 11:19 says the same thing by grouping. The quotation alone (8:32-33) is the same words as Isa 53:7-8 and takes no side. (The drafter's account says 'no line saying one passage is about another'; as written, Acts 8:34-35 is that line.)
concepts.why: OT beside NT: Jewish and secular readers (Isa 53 read of Israel, of the prophet, of the servant) and the Reformed / Baptist reader (Isa 53 messianic) both need the grouping to stay at the quotation. Isa 53:10 and 53:12 do not themselves say lamb or slaughter; they are the same chapter, so keep them, but the name is Isa 53:7's. Notes are exact.

note_fixes: Romans 5:9-11: trim to Romans 5:9-10; verse 11 (rejoicing, 'received reconciliation') is not about blood or death
concepts.why: Original arbitrates / secular scholar: Acts 20:28 rests on contested ground. The manuscripts differ ('church of God' / 'of the Lord'), and the Greek 'tou haimatos tou idiou' can be 'His own blood' or 'the blood of His own [Son]'. A concept on 'His blood' should not stand on the BSB's choice among them when seven other passages carry it without doubt. Atonement: none of the passages names a theory (ransom, satisfaction, victory); 'purchased', 'redemption', 'reconciled', 'peace', 'released' are the texts' words and are left unranked, which all nine readers can accept.

concepts.name: The sacrifice and service of your faith
concepts.why: Name vs passages: 'living' is Rom 12:1's word; Phil 2:17 and 2 Tim 4:6 are a drink offering poured out (Paul's own life, and in 2 Tim 4:6 his approaching death), Heb 13:16 is doing good and sharing, 1 Pet 2:5 is spiritual sacrifices. Phil 2:17's own phrase, 'the sacrifice and service of your faith', covers all five (Rom 12:1 'your spiritual service of worship'). Catholic/Orthodox (the Eucharistic sacrifice) and Protestant (the priesthood of all) readers can accept either, but only under a name that does not choose among the senses of 'priesthood' in 1 Pet 2:5. Notes are exact.

concepts.name: He will be forgiven, and the offerings will please the LORD
concepts.why: Name vs passages, and the hope rule: 'And he will be forgiven' is said by Lev 4:31, Num 15:25-26, Heb 10:17-18 and 1 John 1:7 (cleanses). Ps 51:17, Mal 1:11 and Mal 3:3-4 speak of acceptance ('will not despise', 'pure offerings', 'will please the LORD'), not forgiveness. Either rename to cover both (Mal 3:4's own words 'will please the LORD' are the texts' hope as much as forgiveness is) or move the three. Mal 1:11 is read by Catholic and Orthodox readers as the Eucharist, by Protestants as the worship of the nations, by Jewish readers as the nations honouring the one God; placed here with no note it takes no side, and must stay with no note. The hope is still the last concept and nothing dark was dropped for it; but the OT hope for sacrifice itself, 'their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar' (Isa 56:7), is missing (see missing) and is the nearest match to Mal 3:4.

secondary_or_links: Secondary 'Burnt offerings -> the place the LORD will choose': Exodus 20:24 says 'in every place where I cause My name to be remembered', the opposite emphasis from Deut 12:5-6, 13-14 ('the place the LORD will choose', 'not in just any place'). Putting both under one label harmonises two texts the corpus leaves in tension (scholars and Jewish readers know this as the altar-law tension). Drop Exod 20:24 from this row or relabel the row 'Where to offer' so each stands in its own words.
Secondary 'The altar -> whatever touches it will be holy': Matt 23:19 says the altar makes the gift sacred, Exod 29:37 that whatever touches it is holy. These agree; keep.
Secondary 'Sacrifices of righteousness': Ps 51:19 lives here while concept 17 quotes only Ps 51:16-17; see concept 17. Mal 3:3 appears here and in concept 27; harmless overlap.

Lev 16:8-10 (concept 12): the BSB's 'scapegoat' renders the Hebrew 'azazel', a word whose meaning scholars and Jewish readers hold open. The note is an exact quotation of the BSB, so it stands, but nothing on the card should explain the word.
Luke 22:20 (concept 15): a minority of manuscripts omit Luke 22:19b-20; Matt 26:28 and 1 Cor 11:25 carry the same words, so nothing rests on the verse. Optional: keep as is.

Order: concepts 22, 23, 24, 25 run Isa 53, Lamb of God, By His blood, Once for all without a break, and read to a Jewish or secular reader as a chain from prophecy to fulfilment. Each concept is in the texts' words, so no change is demanded; but do not add any note or sub-heading that connects 22 to 23, and consider ordering so that 21 and 22 are not the only bridge from the OT block to the NT block.

Links: 'Messiah/Christology' is the only link whose name is a doctrinal term. It is a theme's name, and an honest link where passages overlap (Isa 53, John 1:29, Heb 7-10), so keep it, but let no card say why it is linked beyond the shared references.

The Lord's Supper: concept 15 gives Matt 26:28 and Luke 22:20 as the words, with no word on what the cup is; that is the right posture (Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed, Baptist and Pentecostal readers part on exactly this). If 1 Cor 10:16-21 or 11:23-26 are ever added, give the verses and no framing line. Atonement: concepts 11, 24 and 25 name no theory; keep it that way. 1 John 2:2 ('the whole world', concept 11) is a verse Reformed and Wesleyan readers argue over; it is shown only in its own words, which is correct.

missing.why: The texts repeatedly show an offering received by fire from the LORD (Aaron, Gideon, Elijah, Solomon's dedication). A reader of this theme would expect it; it is wholly in the texts' words and takes no side.

missing.sub_theme: I will not offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing
missing.why: David buys the threshing floor and refuses a free offering; the text develops the cost of the offering, and the same site (Moriah) carries Gen 22 and 2 Chr 3:1.

missing.sub_theme: Strange fire, and contempt for the LORD's offering
missing.why: The outline has the prophets' hard words (concept 20) and the nations' sacrifices (secondary), but not the priests' own failures in the offering, which the narrative plainly records; it is also the dark counterpart to 'a pleasing aroma' and keeps the theme honest.
Freewill and vow offerings are named alongside peace offerings in concept 7 and Deut 12:6 but never as their own thing; Ps 66:13-15 and Lev 22:21 are the texts that speak of them directly.

missing.sub_theme: Their burnt offerings and sacrifices will be accepted on My altar
missing.why: The hope concept (27) lacks the prophets' word that sacrifice itself is restored, and this is the nearest match to Mal 1:11 and 3:3-4 already in it; Baptist (dispensational) readers expect it to be there and others will not mind. Ezekiel 40-48 is the contested one (literal temple sacrifices, symbol, or Jewish expectation); leave it out unless words only are quoted with no timing.
Home for 1 Cor 10:18 once it leaves concept 7: the texts plainly speak of eating from the offerings (the offerer's portion, the priests' portion). Under this name it says only what the verses say.
